BPV-1 and BPV-2, the most frequent papillomaviruses in cattle, play a role in the pathogenesis of mesenchyma tumors of the urinary tract.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
BPV-1 and BPV-2 are the two most prevalent bovine papillomaviruses and that they are associated with the majority of bovine urinary bladder tumors, which are mostly hemangiomas and/or angiosarcomata.
BPV-1 and BPV-2 can infect and cause tumors in the bladder epithelium and mesenchyma, respectively.
bovine papillomavirus-2 (BPV-2) is a ubiquitous infection that can be transmitted to cattle through bracken fern and that it can cause mesenchymal and epithelial tumors of the urinary bladders.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the bovine urinary bladder is a target organ for BPV-2 infection, and the virus is able to induce mesenchymal neoplastic lesions.
the BPV2 is a ubiquitous virus that can infect both epithelial and non-epithelial cells and that its oncogenic potential can lead to the development of both epithelial and vascular tumors.
BPV-1 and BPV-2 have a broad host range, infecting not only epithelial cells, but also mesenchymal ones.
